title: SECTION 1, UNIT 2
subtitle: Identify phonetic and orthographic look-alike/sound-alike brand medication counterparts (Accupril/Aciphex, Activase/TNKase) from ISMP.

lasaPairs.feature: Shared initial Ac- and syllable cadence; middle -cupril vs -ciphex
Shared initial A- and ending -t/-x sound cadence
Cathflo prefix modifier for low-dose 2mg catheter clearance
Shared suffix -ase with distinct roots Activ- vs TNK-
Adacel (Tdap booster) vs Daptacel (DTaP pediatric primary)

levels.title: Brand LASA Pair Recognition
levels.description: Recognize confusable brand medication counterparts sharing phonetics and syllable structures.
levels.learningObjective: Identify documented ISMP brand-name look-alike and sound-alike counterparts.

activities.learningObjective: Identify documented Look-Alike / Sound-Alike brand counterparts.

questions.prompt: Which medication is a documented Look-Alike / Sound-Alike counterpart to Accupril?
questions.explanation: Accupril (quinapril) and Aciphex (rabeprazole) share sound-alike brand names and can be easily confused in verbal orders.

questions.prompt: Which medication is an ISMP-documented sound-alike counterpart to Aciphex?
questions.explanation: Aciphex (rabeprazole) and Aricept (donepezil) share acoustic cadence and initial letter A-.

questions.prompt: Which thrombolytic medication is a documented look-alike / sound-alike counterpart to Activase?
questions.explanation: Activase (alteplase) and TNKase (tenecteplase) are both thrombolytics sharing the '-ase' suffix and confusable dosing.

questions.prompt: Which vaccine formulation is the sound-alike and look-alike counterpart to Adacel (Tdap)?
questions.explanation: Adacel (Tdap booster) and Daptacel (DTaP pediatric) share similar sounds and acronyms with different patient age indications.

levels.title: Brand Formulation Discrimination
levels.description: Differentiate product modifiers and sound-alike brand pairs on the ISMP list.
levels.learningObjective: Differentiate brand modifiers (Cathflo) and look-alike brand names (Aldara/Alora).

activities.learningObjective: Distinguish specific brand qualifiers and look-alike pairs.

questions.prompt: Which brand product modifier distinguishes the 2 mg catheter clearance formulation of alteplase from standard systemic Activase?
questions.explanation: Cathflo Activase is specifically formulated as a 2 mg dose for restoring catheter patency, distinct from systemic Activase vials.

questions.prompt: Which transdermal product is an ISMP look-alike / sound-alike counterpart to the topical cream Aldara?
questions.explanation: Aldara (imiquimod cream) and Alora (estradiol patch) differ by only one interior letter (-d- vs -o-) and have completely distinct clinical indications.

questions.prompt: Which medication is a documented sound-alike counterpart to Aricept on the ISMP list?
questions.explanation: Aciphex and Aricept are documented sound-alike counterparts on the ISMP list.

levels.title: Brand Pair Memorization & Discrimination
levels.description: Reinforce memory recall and distinction across all Unit 2 brand-name LASA pairs.
levels.learningObjective: Accurately recall and discriminate confusable brand medication counterparts from memory.

activities.learningObjective: Discriminate brand pairs and identify exact counterpart designations.

questions.prompt: Which thrombolytic medication pairs with TNKase on the ISMP list of confused drug names?
questions.explanation: TNKase (tenecteplase) and Activase (alteplase) are direct look-alike / sound-alike counterparts on the ISMP list.

questions.prompt: Which vaccine is the confusable look-alike / sound-alike counterpart to Daptacel (DTaP)?
questions.explanation: Daptacel (DTaP) and Adacel (Tdap) are documented ISMP confusable pairs.

questions.prompt: Which topical product is the look-alike counterpart to Alora?
questions.explanation: Alora and Aldara are look-alike counterparts differing by only a single interior letter.

levels.title: Unit 2 Mastery
levels.description: Comprehensive review of Unit 2 brand-name LASA pairs followed by an unassisted brand recognition capstone task.
levels.learningObjective: Demonstrate complete unit mastery of brand-name LASA pairs and accurate counterpart identification.

activities.learningObjective: Review brand-name LASA relationships across Unit 2.

questions.prompt: Which medication is paired with Accupril on the ISMP list of confused drug names?
questions.explanation: Accupril and Aciphex are sound-alike brand counterparts on the ISMP list.

questions.prompt: Which drug pairs with Activase on the ISMP list of confused drug names?
questions.explanation: Activase and TNKase are documented look-alike thrombolytic counterparts.

activities.learningObjective: Independently identify the exact look-alike counterpart to Aldara without scaffolding.

questions.prompt: UNIT MASTERY CAPSTONE TASK: Which medication is the documented ISMP look-alike / sound-alike counterpart to Aldara?
questions.explanation: Alora and Aldara form a high-risk look-alike pair differing only in interior orthography.
